label: Saturday, October 31, 2026 · Worst month since March day edition
intro: Good morning. It's Saturday, October 31st. Here's your Read Daily brief.

items.title: Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 clobbered as October closes with brutal sell-off
items.take: Friday was brutal: the Nasdaq fell 2.86%, its worst day since June 5, the S&P lost 1.82%, and October closed as the Nasdaq’s worst month since March 2025 (it shed 5.3%). Amazon and Intel earnings stoked fresh doubts about the enormous cost of the AI boom.

items.title: Running Scared: Amazon, Intel Put Tech on Defense
items.take: The Amazon numbers are the crux: AWS grew 39%, above forecasts, yet the company still ran negative free cash flow while holding 2026 capex at about $220 billion. The same math that sank Alphabet. Intel blamed weak PC demand even as its data center and AI revenue grew 78% to $7.3 billion.

items.title: Google Stock Hammered After Earnings Raise AI Revenue Concerns
items.take: Google finished the week down 13% as investors weigh how much AI is eating, rather than feeding, its search business. That single question now frames the whole tape: the market is repricing what AI capex actually buys.

items.title: Midterms, Apple earnings, jobs report. Wall Street faces a big week ahead just as investors dump tech
items.take: A heavy calendar hits an AI-wary market: Apple reports Monday, Election Day is Tuesday, and the October jobs report lands Friday. Roughly half the S&P has reported so far, with Q3 earnings on pace to rise 31.6%.

items.title: Hack is likely largest theft of digital currencies in history
items.take: The Binance hack is now estimated at $6.3 billion, likely the largest crypto theft ever, and investigators watched thousands of automated transactions move the funds across blockchains. Crypto stocks fell more than 6% on the news Friday.

items.title: Thoughts on the Market: The Curious Calm of Credit Markets
items.take: Today’s rotation pick looks at the interesting wrinkle in Friday’s rout: stocks clobbered, credit markets oddly calm. That calm is the tell traders are watching, since real credit stress would turn an equity story into a credit one.
